The dossiers sit inside Cliopatria's Greek City-States or Mycenaean Greece aggregates and must be carved out of them by the renderer.

WebFetch answers through a summarising model, not raw text: every quote in the dossiers is the extract it returned for a dated-sentence prompt; the reviewer should spot-check against the page. On pages it called thin or silent, the dossier records confidence 1 or the page's silence.

Most shapes are researcher's readings (discs round a city, an admin-1 for a named river-bounded area) because Wikipedia gives areas or boundaries for few ancient states; areas that the pages do give (Pylos 2,000 km2, Akragas about 3,500 km2, Mycenae two to three times a palatial state) are matched by the discs.
